decisions.rationale: Names a single, specific inherited complement disorder (C5 deficiency); the 'Hereditary' qualifier does not change it into a family of diseases, so it is parallel to the C7 deficiency example.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 1 (Specific Disease); Examples 6 (C7 deficiency)

decisions.rationale: Discoid lupus erythematosus is a specific, well-defined form of lupus with no further categorization needed in this mention.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 1 (Specific Disease); Examples 1 and 5 (minimum span, specific named disease)

decisions.rationale: Second occurrence of the same specific disease name in the abstract; duplicate mentions are annotated separately.
Hypocomplementemia describes a laboratory finding (low complement activity) rather than a named disease entity; it is an abnormality-type general term that is excluded.
decisions.guideline_section: What NOT to Annotate 4 (Do not annotate general terms such as abnormalities)

decisions.rationale: Refers to the specific condition of C5 deficiency (selective deficiency of one complement component); the phrase is a specific disease mention, not just the generic word deficiency.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 1 (Specific Disease); Examples 6 (C7 deficiency)

decisions.rationale: 'Deficient' is a generic adjective describing the child's state and does not name a disease; the word deficiency-type terms are excluded as general terms.
decisions.guideline_section: What NOT to Annotate 4 (Do not annotate general terms such as deficiency)

decisions.rationale: A contiguous string joining two separate diseases (discoid lupus erythematosus and C5 deficiency) that cannot be split without losing information about the association.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 2 (Contiguous text strings / Composite Mention); Examples 7 (composite of several Specific Diseases)
